articles.title: 'Play according to the situation': Aaryavir Sehwag reveals Virat Kohli inspiration after finishing as U19 Asia Cup's top run-scorer
articles.summary: Carrying the Sehwag surname comes with its own expectations, but young India batter Aaryavir Sehwag is keen to carve out his identity by focusing on what
articles.body: Carrying the Sehwag surname comes with its own expectations, but young India batter Aaryavir Sehwag is keen to carve out his identity by focusing on what the team needs rather than sticking to a particular batting style. The 17-year-old has found inspiration in Virat Kohli, whose ability to adapt to match situations and take responsibility has shaped his own approach to batting.Aaryavir enjoyed a memorable campaign at the ACC Under-19 Asia Cup in Oman, finishing as the tournament's leading run-scorer with 361 runs in five matches. His tally included a century and three half-centuries, performances that earned him the Player of the Tournament award as India lifted their ninth title with a thrilling one-wicket victory over Pakistan in the final.The youngster's ability to adapt to different conditions and build his innings according to the team's requirements stood out throughout the competition. Speaking to JioStar, Aaryavir opened up about his admiration for Kohli and explained why he does not want to be labelled as a particular type of batter.'I am a huge Virat Kohli fan': Aaryavir on his batting philosophyAaryavir said Kohli's approach to batting has inspired him to assess situations carefully and adjust his game according to the team's requirements. Rather than identifying himself as an aggressive stroke-maker or an accumulator, the youngster wants to remain flexible and play according to the demands of the match."I don't label myself as a stroke player or any kind of player. I just want to play according to the situation. As I've said earlier, I am a huge Virat Kohli fan, and I want to do what the team requires and needs at that time. I'm glad that I could play the way I did," he told JioStar.Aaryavir Sehwag recalls challenging conditions during 160-run knock against UAEAaryavir smashed 160 off 168 deliveries, including 17 fours and seven sixes, to help India post 309/7 against the UAE. India eventually secured a 70-run victory to book their place in the semifinals. Reflecting on the innings, the youngster revealed that negotiating the initial seam movement was a key part of his plan. However, the pitch also offered unexpected turn, making batting challenging even after the opening overs."Initially, those 10 to 15 overs have always been a challenge in Oman throughout the Asia Cup. In those first 10 to 15 overs, the plan was to see off the seam movement, and after that, shockingly, there was turn as well in that match against UAE. It was a strange kind of wicket, but I'm glad that I could spend a good amount of time on that wicket and once I got set, I just kept batting, and the runs kept coming," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India boycott trophy ceremony after Pakistan handed Blind Asia Cup title following washout
articles.summary: MUMBAI: A massive controversy erupted on Friday after Pakistan were declared the winners of the Men's Blind Cricket Asia Cup 2026 in Dhaka, despite the
articles.body: MUMBAI: A massive controversy erupted on Friday after Pakistan were declared the winners of the Men's Blind Cricket Asia Cup 2026 in Dhaka, despite the much-anticipated final against India being completely washed out.The match referee, Tamim from Bangladesh, declared Pakistan the champions on the basis of their superior Net Run Rate (NRR) in the league stage. However, the Indian team has disputed the decision, claiming that this clause was never mentioned in the tournament's playing conditions provided to them.India subsequently boycotted the trophy presentation ceremony and rejected the match referee's decision to award the title to Pakistan.India had earlier lost to Pakistan in the league stage in a thrilling last-over encounter."It's completely unfair. It's been raining here in Dhaka since yesterday because of a cyclone. The final was supposed to start at 11:30 am. However, the match didn't start at all. As per match rules, we were at the ground (ABG Sports City ground in Dhaka). However, at 4:15 pm, the match was abandoned due to rain and the match referee declared Pakistan the winner due to a better Net Run Rate in the league stage."This rule was never mentioned to us in the playing conditions provided to us, or mentioned in the meetings of the match referee with the captains a day before the tournament began. As per the playing conditions, if the match had been tied and a Super Over was played and that also remained tied, then the winner being decided on the Net Run Rate rule would've been applicable."Nowhere in the history of cricket has one team been declared the winner despite the final being abandoned without a ball being bowled! Neither the ICC nor the MCC rules have such a rule in place in case the final of a tournament is washed out. It's clear that the laws have been twisted to declare Pakistan the tournament winners. Both the teams should have been declared joint winners, or the final should've been played on a reserve day," Dhiraj Sequeira, manager of the Indian blind team, told TOI from Dhaka."We appealed against the decision to award Pakistan the trophy to the technical committee of the tournament, but they too rejected our appeal, despite two members of the panel being in favour of our appeal. Consequently, we decided to boycott the presentation ceremony, after consulting CABI," Sequeira added."CABI is not too hopeful of getting any 'justice' from the World Blind Cricket Council (WBCC), as its president is Pakistan's Syed Sultan Shah, who is also the president/chairman of the Pakistan Blind Cricket Council.""Pakistan made the match referee declare the result in their favour, despite the final being totally washed out? How is this possible? I feel very ashamed about it. It's a dark day in the history of blind cricket. A trophy has been awarded to Pakistan, which they don't deserve to win at all. They should feel ashamed to carry this trophy."The organisers never conveyed this rule to us previously, and neither does such a rule of declaring a tournament winner exist. This is a self-made, last-minute rule. We've not accepted this result. Hence, we boycotted the presentation ceremony. I am completely disappointed."We would've been happy if they had beaten India in the final. We don't care. Winning and losing is always a part of the game. In the league match, they defeated us on the last ball (players from both sides shook hands too). That's fine. It was such a wonderful match. We were very happy about it. We accepted it. If they had played and won, we would have gracefully accepted the result," Mahantesh GK, president of the Cricket Association for the Blind in India (CABI), told TOI."We (India's men's and women's blind teams) are considering abstaining from playing against Pakistan in global tournaments (for the blind) from now on," he asserted.In a strongly worded statement issued on Friday, CABI condemned the decision to declare Pakistan the sole winners of the Men's Blind Cricket Asia Cup 2026 after the final against India was washed out due to rain.CABI categorically rejected the decision, maintaining that India and Pakistan should be recognised as joint winners.According to CABI, Section 27 of the tournament's technical regulations deals specifically with a tied final, with both sentences referring to that situation. CABI said it raised this interpretation with the World Blind Cricket Council (WBCC) Technical Committee, which initially agreed to declare both teams joint winners.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Selectors are making a blunder': Krishnamachari Srikkanth questions India's handling of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
articles.summary: Former India captain and chief selector Krishnamachari Srikkanth has launched a strong criticism of the selectors and team management over their handling
articles.body: Former India captain and chief selector Krishnamachari Srikkanth has launched a strong criticism of the selectors and team management over their handling of teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, insisting that the youngster deserves a consistent run in the Indian side. Srikkanth believes the 15-year-old has the potential to become a match-winner across formats and even play a significant role in reviving Test cricket globally.Speaking at the sports event on Friday, Srikkanth said the selectors and team management were making a mistake by not providing Sooryavanshi with enough opportunities.'They are discouraging him': Srikkanth slams selectors over Sooryavanshi's treatmentSrikkanth questioned the decision to pick Sooryavanshi for one match and then leave him out for several games, stressing that the youngster needed sustained opportunities to prove his abilities."What they (selectors and team management) are doing with him is not right. They are not encouraging him; they are discouraging him, which is not done. These guys are making a blunder. They play him for one match, they don't play him for five matches. That's not done. Sad," Srikkanth said at the event.'Test cricket revival happens all over the world': Srikkanth backs Sooryavanshi's potentialGoing a step further, Srikkanth suggested that Sooryavanshi's success in the longest format could generate renewed interest in Test cricket, not just in India but across the cricketing world."If Sooryavanshi clicks in Test cricket, a Test cricket revival happens all over the world, not just for India, all over the world. Today in New Zealand, when he was playing the T20 matches, people came all the way -- a full crowd -- to watch Sooryavanshi bat. Wherever he goes, everybody comes to watch Sooryavanshi bat," he said.He called on the selectors to show faith in the youngster and give him a sustained run instead of making frequent changes to his selection."This boy has done so brilliantly for you -- let him play all the matches. Do you mean to say he is not good enough to play Test or One Day cricket? He is 100 per cent sure to play good One Day cricket. Give him 20 innings, tell him he won't get dropped -- you do whatever you want. That boy will win five to seven matches single-handedly for you."And if he scores in Test cricket, the whole world will start reviving Test cricket everywhere, in any part of the world," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asia Cup Rising Stars: India A crush Nepal by 306 runs after bowling them out for 26
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India A registered a staggering 306-run victory over Nepal in their opening match of the ACC Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026, producing a
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India A registered a staggering 306-run victory over Nepal in their opening match of the ACC Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026, producing a dominant all-round performance at the West End Park International Cricket Stadium in Doha.After posting 332/9 in 50 overs, India A's bowlers delivered a sensational performance to dismiss Nepal for just 26 in 11.3 overs. Nepal's total is the fourth-lowest in List A cricket history.Tilak Varma, Kushagra power India A to 332Batting first, India A recovered from a few early setbacks through a magnificent 206-run partnership between captain Tilak Varma and wicketkeeper-batter Kumar Kushagra.Kushagra smashed 117 off 102 deliveries, including 10 fours and five sixes, while Varma scored 107 off 113 balls, hitting six fours and four sixes. Both batters registered centuries to put India A in a commanding position.Suryansh Shedge provided the finishing fireworks with an unbeaten 36 off just 14 balls, featuring four sixes and a boundary, as India A finished on 332/9. For Nepal, Lalit Rajbanshi and Sandeep Lamichhane picked up three wickets each.Rana and Prince trigger historic Nepal collapseNepal's chase never got going as Harshit Rana and Prince Yadav exploited the conditions brilliantly, generating considerable swing and seam movement.Returning from injury, Rana looked in excellent rhythm, striking in the opening over by trapping Arjun Kumal lbw for a duck. Prince then dismissed Deepak Dumre and bowled Basir Ahamad as Nepal slipped to 1-3 inside two overs.The collapse continued as Rana and Prince kept finding breakthroughs. Rana finished with four wickets for 16 runs in six overs, while Prince produced a sensational five-wicket haul, conceding just six runs in five overs.Shahbaz Ahmed claimed the final wicket, stumping Nandan Yadav for 2, as Nepal were bundled out for 26. The result sealed a remarkable 306-run win for India A.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'We didn't have our full-strength team here': Nepal captain Lamichhane after 306-run defeat to India A
articles.summary: Nepal captain Sandeep Lamichhane admitted his side were completely outplayed by India A, while pointing to the absence of several first-choice players as
articles.body: Nepal captain Sandeep Lamichhane admitted his side were completely outplayed by India A, while pointing to the absence of several first-choice players as a challenge ahead of their Asia Cup Rising Stars campaign."We were outplayed today. Credit goes to the way the Indian team carried their momentum. We had a good start with the ball, but they utilised their skills. Credit to Tilak and Kumar for the way they handled the pressure," Lamichhane said after the match.The Nepal skipper also revealed that the team were dealing with availability issues, with several players arriving in Doha on the morning of the match due to the ongoing Nepal Premier League (NPL) back home."We didn't have our full-strength team here. A few of the players arrived this morning. NPL is going on back home. We somehow had to manage and put some new faces for this tournament. It was really a hard task for us to manage everything," he added.Despite the heavy defeat, Lamichhane remained confident about Nepal's prospects in the upcoming matches, insisting that the team understood where they had fallen short."But we all are going in the right direction. We are still fully confident about how we're going to approach the upcoming games. We know where we lacked today," he said, reiterating that India A deserved full credit for their performance.Rana, Prince Yadav dismantle Nepal for 26India A’s pace duo of Harshit Rana and Prince Yadav produced a sensational bowling performance to bundle out Nepal for just 26 in 11.3 overs, sealing a massive 306-run victory in their opening match of the Asia Cup Rising Stars 50-over tournament on Friday.Chasing a daunting target of 333, Nepal’s innings fell apart from the outset. Rana struck in the third ball, trapping Arjun Kamal leg-before without scoring, and the wickets continued to tumble. Nepal were reduced to 17 for five by the seventh over as the Indian pacers exploited the pace and swing on offer.Rana finished with impressive figures of 4/16, while Prince was even more devastating, claiming 5/6. The pair accounted for nine of Nepal’s 10 wickets, leaving India A skipper Tilak Varma with no need to use his other bowling options.Left-arm spinner Shahbaz Ahmed picked up the remaining wicket. Nepal’s batting collapse was complete when they were bowled out for 26, with none of their batters managing to reach double figures.Earlier, centuries from Varma (107) and Kumar Kushagra (117) had powered India A to 332 for nine.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India A create history with biggest List A victory by runs, hammer Nepal by 306 runs in Rising Stars Asia Cup
articles.summary: India A produced a record-breaking performance in their opening match of the ACC Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026, thrashing Nepal by 306 runs at the West
articles.body: India A produced a record-breaking performance in their opening match of the ACC Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026, thrashing Nepal by 306 runs at the West End Park International Cricket Stadium on Friday. The emphatic victory, built on centuries from captain Tilak Varma and Kumar Kushagra before a sensational bowling display, marked India A’s biggest-ever win by runs in List A cricket.After posting a formidable 332/9 in their 50 overs, India A bundled Nepal out for a mere 26 in 11.3 overs to seal a dominant victory and make a strong statement in the tournament.India A's biggest List A victories by runsIndia A's 306-run victory over Nepal is their biggest win by runs in List A cricket. Here are the four other major victories identified in the available historical record listings:RankWinning marginOpponentYear1306 runsNepal20262281 runsLeicestershire20183203 runsWest Indies A20184202 runsNetherlands A2006Tilak Varma, Kumar Kushagra power India A to 332Put in to bat, India A suffered a few early setbacks but recovered through a magnificent 206-run partnership between Tilak Varma and Kumar Kushagra. Both batters went on to score centuries, taking the innings away from Nepal.Kushagra smashed 117 off 102 deliveries, including 10 fours and five sixes, while captain Tilak contributed 107 off 113 balls, with six fours and four sixes. Suryansh Shedge provided the late fireworks with an unbeaten 36 off just 14 deliveries, striking four sixes and a boundary to help India A finish at 332/9. For Nepal, Lalit Rajbanshi and Sandeep Lamichhane picked up three wickets apiece.Harshit Rana, Prince Yadav dismantle NepalNepal's chase never got going as India's pace attack made early inroads. Harshit Rana struck in the opening over, dismissing Arjun Kumal for a duck, before Prince Yadav joined the demolition act. Prince removed Deepak Dumre and bowled Basir Ahamad as Nepal slipped to 1/3 inside the first two overs. The wickets continued to tumble as the Indian bowlers maintained relentless pressure.Prince finished with remarkable figures of 5/6 from five overs, while Rana claimed 4/16 in six overs. Shahbaz Ahmed picked up the final wicket, stumping Nandan Yadav for two, as Nepal were dismissed for just 26 in 11.3 overs.Nepal record fifth-lowest total in List A cricketNepal's total of 26 is the fifth-lowest completed innings score in men's List A cricket history. The four lower totals on record are West Indies Under-19's 18 against Barbados in 2007, Saracens Sports Club's 19 against Colts Cricket Club in 2012, Middlesex's 23 against Yorkshire in 1974 and Oman's 24 against Scotland in 2019.The collapse also underlined the scale of India's dominance, with Nepal managing to last only 11.3 overs in their pursuit of 333. The 306-run margin, meanwhile, stands as India A's biggest victory by runs in List A cricket, giving the side a memorable start to their Rising Stars Asia Cup campaign.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: James Anderson: England legend loses Italia T10 league debut for Napoli Knights in first match since Lancashire exit
articles.summary: James Anderson was released by Lancashire at the end of the County Championship season and has joined Surrey in 2027; Anderson is among the players in action for Napoli Knights, a T10 franchise league in Italy
articles.body:
Anderson is co-owner of Napoli Knights, with the 44-year-old's appearance his first since being released by boyhood club Lancashire at the end of the season.

Napoli Knights are one of six teams in the nine-day tournament at Roma Cricket Ground, running until November 28, with Anderson's side restricted to 73-9 after losing the toss and batting first.

Anderson finished nought not out from one delivery faced, scampering a bye from the final ball of the innings, before taking 0-14 from two overs during Rome Gladiators' successful chase.

England's history-making Test bowler conceded just three from a tight opening over of Rome's chase, before being hit down the ground by Singh for a maximum - during an 11-run over - when returning for a second stint later in the innings.

Anthony Mosca fired an unbeaten 45 from 27 deliveries and Jaspreet Singh ended 15 not out from nine, as Rome Gladiators claimed a five-wicket win with two balls remaining.

Wayne Madsen, captaining the Napoli Knights: "It's fantastic to have Jimmy [Anderson] here. He's inspirational to so many of us.

"To be playing with him, and for him to share his knowledge with this group, is amazing. I think, as we've seen, he has still got the skill to go out there and perform at the top level."

Napoli Knights have further matches against Brescia Lions (Saturday), Venice Livewire (Sunday), Milan Icons (Monday) and Bologna Hurricanes (TBC).

Anderson has joined Surrey ahead of the 2027 season in the Rothesay County Championship, having been left "sad" and "quite shocked" by his contract not being extended by Lancashire .

Upon the announcement of his move to the Kia Oval, Anderson said: "It's an honour to join a club like Surrey and I can't wait to start a new chapter in my career. I still feel like I have a lot to offer, taking wickets, trying to help the team win games of cricket.

"I also think that I can bring a lot to the team off the field and help those young players who are looking to develop their skillset and go on and represent their country."

Anderson, who turns 45 in July of next year, will get the opportunity to add to his haul of 1,193 first-class wickets and perhaps more silverware to a glittering CV.

articles.title: 'It was not easy to score runs': Tilak Varma after India A’s 306-run victory over Nepal
articles.summary: India A captain Tilak Varma was pleased with his side’s performance after their emphatic 306-run win over Nepal in the Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament,
articles.body: India A captain Tilak Varma was pleased with his side’s performance after their emphatic 306-run win over Nepal in the Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament, while praising his partnership with Kumar Kushagra.Varma said the pitch was challenging for batting and that the duo wanted to take their partnership deep, knowing it would be difficult for new batters to settle in.“The wicket was slightly challenging. It was not easy to score runs. But the way me and Kumar played, really proud,” he said after the match.The pair added 206 runs for the fourth wicket, with Varma scoring 107 and Kushagra making 117. The skipper revealed they had discussed targeting a total of around 280 before Suryansh Shedge’s late unbeaten 36 off 14 balls lifted India A to 332/9.Varma also praised Harshit Rana’s return from injury, saying it was important for the bowler to deliver such a performance.Looking ahead to the clash against Pakistan A, Varma said India would focus on their basics, adding, “Just another game for us.”India A crush Nepal by 306 runs in Asia Cup Rising Stars openerTilak Varma and Kumar Kushagra hit centuries before Harshit Rana and Prince Yadav demolished Nepal's batting line-up.India A began their Asia Cup Rising Stars 50-over campaign with a commanding 306-run victory over Nepal on Friday, thanks to brilliant centuries from captain Tilak Varma and wicketkeeper Kumar Kushagra.After being put in to bat, India A recovered from early setbacks through a 206-run partnership between Varma and Kushagra. Varma scored 107 off 113 balls, while Kushagra smashed 117 off 102 deliveries, helping India A post an imposing 332 for nine. Suryansh Shedge added late momentum with an unbeaten 36 off just 14 balls.Nepal's bowlers Lalit Rajbanshi and Sandeep Lamichhane claimed three wickets each, while Nandan Yadav picked up two.However, Nepal's chase quickly turned into a disaster as India's fast bowlers Harshit Rana and Prince Yadav ripped through their batting line-up. Rana finished with figures of 4/16, while Prince delivered a sensational spell of 5/6, bowling Nepal out for just 26 in 11.3 overs.Nepal lost their first wicket without scoring and slipped to 17 for five by the seventh over. None of their batters managed to reach double figures. Shahbaz Ahmed claimed the remaining wicket as India A completed a dominant all-round performance.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Josh Hazlewood defends Pat Cummins over 'Sandpapergate' and backs Australia's Test captain to continue after "pile-on"
articles.summary: Australia captain Pat Cummins has been scrutinised after Cameron Bancroft's damning account of the 2018 sandpaper scandal; Josh Hazlewood defended Cummins in a new interview and questioned how the Test team would react if he was forced to step away as captain
articles.body:
Cameron Bancroft plunged Australian cricket into further turmoil with a 4,000-word statement, backing claims "the whole team" knew about the plot and contradicting strong denials Cummins offered in his press conference a few days earlier.

Cummins had branded Khawaja's testimony "complete and utter nonsense" and "100 per cent wrong", leading Bancroft to go public with his story, while Australia's Test captain has had his future speculated after how he has handled the incident.

"It feels like it's been a bit of a pile on the last few days [at Cummins] from different people," Hazlewood told CodeSports . "I want to back Pat [Cummins] and everything he said in his press conference last week, everything he's done for the last five or six years in particular as captain.

"To get the group where it is now and in a position where something like that [sandpaper] is never going to happen again - I think is just a remarkable job. He's a great leader. If you went around and asked everyone in the team, you'd hear the same response.

"If we turned up for the first Test and he wasn't the captain and it was someone else, honestly, I don't know how that would go."

Australia are next in Test action when they face New Zealand in a four-match series, beginning on December 9 in Perth, where Hazlewood would consider whether to feature if Cummins was no longer captain.

"I'd have to be put in that position to make a decision, but you'd have to think about it, yeah," Hazlewood added.

Hazlewood denies involvement in sandpaper plan

Bancroft, Warner and then-captain Steve Smith all served bans for their role in the ball-tampering plot, while Hazelwood remains adamant on his position that the bowlers did not know about the use of sandpaper.

"We were interviewed straight after [Cape Town] and I trust what I said in that two-three hour interrogation more than anything because it was in the day or two after," Hazlewood explained.

"It was fresh in my mind at that point. Two things stand out for me from what's been said. Was I an architect in the plan to tamper with the ball with sandpaper? And was I aware sandpaper or foreign substances being used on the field?

"The answer is no. When it boils down to it, I think those two points are crucial."

On whether he noticed a change in ball condition during that Test, Hazlewood said: "I never remember looking at the ball and going, 'wow, this is not natural deterioration'. And obviously the umpires didn't either."

Former England captain Michael Atherton said on the Sky Sports Cricket Podcas t he does not expect Cummins to resign from his role as Test skipper.

"He's obviously got a lot of credit in the bank in terms of performance as captain, having transformed the culture and kept Australia at the top of the tree, if you like," Atherton said. "So I don't think there's an immediate threat there."

articles.title: 'Deserved justice': Why India boycotted presentation ceremony after Pakistan won Asia Cup - Explained
articles.summary: The Indian blind cricket team boycotted the presentation ceremony of the men's Asia Cup in Dhaka on Friday after Pakistan were declared champions even
articles.body: The Indian blind cricket team boycotted the presentation ceremony of the men's Asia Cup in Dhaka on Friday after Pakistan were declared champions even though the final was washed out without a ball being bowled. The decision led to a protest from the Cricket Association for the Blind in India (CABI), which said India and Pakistan should have been declared joint winners.Pakistan were awarded the title on the basis of a better net run rate. However, CABI general secretary Shailendra Yadav accused Pakistan of declaring themselves champions without following the position of the World Blind Cricket Council (WBCC) Technical Committee."I am deeply disappointed and strongly condemn the manner in which Pakistan has declared itself the winner of the Blind Cricket Asia Cup final without a single ball being bowled," Yadav said in a statement.Why did India protest Pakistan's title win?CABI argued that net run rate could not be used to decide the winner of a final that did not begin. According to Yadav, the criterion applied to the qualifying rounds and certain stages of a tournament, but could not automatically determine the outcome of a washed-out final."When rain prevents a single ball from being bowled in a final, the matter must be resolved strictly in accordance with the applicable tournament regulations and the decision of the WBCC Technical Committee."The possible outcomes should be determined through the prescribed provisions, whether that means a reserve day, a shared title or another officially authorised resolution," he said.CABI maintained that the two teams should have been declared joint winners because rain prevented any play in the final.What is CABI's allegation against the WBCC?CABI alleged that WBCC president and Pakistan Blind Cricket Council president Sultan Shah overruled the Technical Committee's decision to declare India and Pakistan joint winners.According to the association, the move forced the match referee to announce Pakistan as champions despite the committee's position.In a social media post, CABI said the decision had overshadowed the tournament's final and reiterated that India "deserved justice".The Indian team stayed away from the presentation ceremony in protest against the decision.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Focus on South Africans, Associates as ILT20 Season 5 prepares to get underway
articles.summary: Dubai: Faf du Plessis, David Miller, Tabraiz Shamsi, Heinrich Klaasen, Lizaad Williams and George Linde must have heaved a collective sigh of relief when
articles.body: Dubai: Faf du Plessis, David Miller, Tabraiz Shamsi, Heinrich Klaasen, Lizaad Williams and George Linde must have heaved a collective sigh of relief when the ILT20 calendar was announced. They might not have been the only ones. With the UAE-based T20 competition starting on November 21 this time -- avoiding an annual clash with South Africa's SA20 in the process -- the South Africans could play in both the competitions.Having played the first three seasons in January-February before moving to December-January last time around, the ILT20 has rescheduled the calendar even further this time. With the tournament now due to play its final on December 20, it will allow the likes of Du Plessis, Miller, Klaasen, Williams and Linde to make their debuts in the UAE.Not just the Proteas. Other players, such as Afghanistan's Rashid Khan, who would otherwise play portion of the ILT20 before jetting off to South Africa, can now play both in their entireties. SA20 Season 5 begins on January 17, 2027."My schedule opened up nicely to have this league open for me. It's always been a goal to come play in the UAE. I'm really looking forward to this competition. It's a strong competition. You just can't walk in here and think you're going to score runs and perform. You really need to be at your best. So that's also the biggest reason why I came to come play this league," said Gulf Giants captain Klaasen.Teammate and fellow South African Miller is equally pleased. "With the schedule for the year, with all the different leagues and international (cricket) and so on, I think it does become quite difficult to schedule these sort of tournaments. I am here, this time, because it's not overlapping with SA20. So I think it's a really good thing. It helps me to be here, so I'm really happy," added Miller.We as South Africans, we analyse the game quite well. We read the game quite well. So I think one of our strong qualities is we're good thinking brains.Over the last five years, the likes of Du Plessis, Quinton de Kock, Klaasen, Reeza Hendricks, Miller and Rilee Rossouw have set the T20 stage on fire, much like the players from the Caribbean did at one point.In tournaments involving more than five teams, Du Plessis has produced 5937 runs in this period; De Kock has blasted 5213 runs, Klaasen has 5066 runs and Hendricks is on 3386 runs. With 300 sixes, Klaasen has also brought the crowd to their feet. As have Du Plessis (273), Dewald Brevis (242) and Rossouw (239)."West Indian cricketers have been blessed with the genuine skills, the natural ability to go after the bowling and they displayed. That's why guys like Chris Gayle and all those guys started playing T20 around the world. So I think for us playing alongside these guys, you get to see what they do as well. We as South Africans, we analyse the game quite well. We read the game quite well. So I think one of our strong qualities is we're good thinking brains. That, with power of playing together and that's a good combination," explained Du Plessis on the eve of the competition.The focus, when Desert Vipers play the MI Emirates in the opener, will not just be on the Proteas. With each squad laden with at least four UAE players, four Afghanistan players, one Ireland player, one player each from Kuwait and Saudi Arabia, plus another from an ICC Associate Member country, it will be a massive learning curve for many.And that will not just be about occupying the dugout. Every playing XI must include at least two UAE players, two Afghanistan players and one Associate player. That last spot can even go to a third UAE player.And the UAE players were in demand at the auction. Muhammad Waseem commanded $210,000 from the MI Emirates. U-19 player Alishan Sharafu had Abu Dhabi Knight Riders shelling out $110,000. Aayan Khan and Muhammad Rohid pocketed $95,000 from Dubai Capitals and ADKR, respectively. USA's Amshi De Silva went to ADKR for $100,000."I think it's a great thing that the Associates has been included as a must-play member as well, because I honestly believe that there's a lot of Associate cricketers that are good enough to play in these leagues, but unfortunately, get overlooked. So it's nice to have Associate players.Sharjah Warriorz's Sikandar Raza finds it to be a useful rule that will allow the Associates to get some exposure and portray their talents."So I think it's going to be a very nice mixture of some unknowns mixed with the knowns. But for me, the most important thing would be who has the skillset to be going at one time looking at the data and matchups," he continued.QUICK SINGLESPlayers to watch🔴Defending champions Desert Vipers boast of Babar Azam, Naseem Shah, Fakhar Zaman, Shadab Khan and Shimron Hetmyer.🔴MI Emirates have Rashid Khan, Nicholas Pooran, Fazalhaq Farooqi and Romario Shepherd.🔴Heinrich Klaasen, David Miller and Liam Livingstone represent the Gulf Giants.🔴Dubai Capitals squad includes Faf du Plessis, Phil Salt, Marcus Stoinis and Mustafizur Rahman.🔴Finn Allen, Sunil Narine, Moeen Ali and Jason Holder will play for the Abu Dhabi Knight Riders.🔴Sharjah Warriorz have James Vince, Sikandar Raza, Mohammad Nabi and Adil Rashid in their midst.WILDCARDS🔴After the retentions and auction, teams were allowed to name their wildcards. And some heavyweights of T20 cricket will play the ILT20 Season 5.🔴ADKR have Andre Russell. Kieron Pollard will turn up for the MI Emirates for a fifth straight season. Tim Seifert is back with the Sharjah Warriorz. Sam Billings is in the Dubai Capitals camp. Akeal Hosein will be with the Gulf Giants while Tom Curran is at the Desert Vipers. NEW RULESBatter zone: ILT20 has introduced a "batter zone" at the popping crease. If the entire ball passes outside this designated area, it will be considered a wide, even if the batter has stepped across the stumps. The existing off-side wide lines and rules still apply to reverse sweeps and switch hits.Shot clock: Earlier, the shot clock applied only to the bowling team; now it will apply to the batting team as well. The batters must be ready for the next over within 60 seconds of the previous one ending. Two warnings will be given per innings. After that, each breach will cost five penalty runs. There are exemptions, however, for injuries, reviews, weather delays and strategic timeouts.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Josh Hazlewood hints at quitting if 'great leader' Pat Cummins loses captaincy as sandpapergate rocks Australia
articles.summary: Australia fast bowler Josh Hazlewood has said he would consider quitting the national team if Pat Cummins were removed as Test captain over allegations
articles.body: Australia fast bowler Josh Hazlewood has said he would consider quitting the national team if Pat Cummins were removed as Test captain over allegations that he knew about the ball-tampering scandal during the 2018 tour of South Africa.Hazlewood backed Cummins after Usman Khawaja, David Warner and, more recently, Cameron Bancroft claimed that “everyone knew” about the use of sandpaper to alter the condition of the ball. The 35-year-old supported Cummins' version of events that he was not involved in the plan.Hazlewood, who has taken 313 Test wickets, had signed a document in 2021 along with Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon, denying any prior knowledge of sandpaper being “taken onto the field”.He described the criticism directed at Cummins since Bancroft published his 4,000-word column earlier this week as “a bit of a pile on” and backed the Australia captain's handling of the issue.“To get the group where it is now and in a position where something like that (sandpaper) is never going to happen again – I think is just a remarkable job,” Hazlewood told Code Sports, as quoted by Fox Sports.“He’s a great leader. If you went around and asked everyone in the team, you’d hear the same response."“I think if we turned up for the first Test and he wasn’t the captain and it was someone else, honestly, I don’t know how that would go.”Australia will face New Zealand in Perth in the first Test of the home summer, starting on December 9.Hazlewood also said he would consider not playing his 82nd Test if Cummins were forced to step down following Bancroft's claim that the Australia captain knew about the ball-tampering eight years ago.“I think I’d have to be put in that position to make a decision, but you’d have to think about it, yeah,” he said.Like Cummins, Hazlewood has publicly stood by his account of the events in 2018, saying he had “no knowledge” of ball-tampering during the South Africa series.“We were interviewed straight after (Cape Town) and I trust what I said in that two-three hour interrogation more than anything because it was in the day or two after,” Hazlewood said.“It was fresh in my mind at that point. Two things stand out for me from what’s been said. Was I an architect in the plan to tamper with the ball with sandpaper? And was I aware (of) sandpaper or foreign substances being used on the field?“The answer is no. When it boils down to it I think those two points are crucial.”The plan to use sandpaper, which was available in the dressing room for players to use on their bats, was first discussed during the tea break on the second day of the second Test at Port Elizabeth, when Australia were behind in the match.In his recent column, Bancroft alleged that then head coach Darren Lehmann and bowling coach David Saker were present when Warner first suggested using sandpaperGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: IND vs NZ 1st Test: Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul lead India's strong reply after New Zealand post 368
articles.summary: There has been constant chatter around Yashasvi Jaiswal’s exclusion from India’s ODI set-up and why he should feature in the 2027 World Cup side.
articles.body: There has been constant chatter around Yashasvi Jaiswal’s exclusion from India’s ODI set-up and why he should feature in the 2027 World Cup side. The young opener has the dual skill of defending and riding out difficult spells before seamlessly counter-attacking, a quality that can be invaluable in the Powerplay.India needed precisely those qualities at the Basin Reserve on Friday. After Henry Nicholls’s unbeaten 175 and Glenn Phillips’s 118 had carried New Zealand to 368 from 70 for five, Jaiswal’s sparkling 85 off 89 balls and KL Rahul’s unbeaten 52 off 116 powered India to 159 for one at stumps. The visitors remain 209 runs behind, but with nine wickets in hand and the pitch having eased considerably, the Test is set up beautifully.India had to go into survival mode early as Matt Henry and Kyle Jamieson bowled four successive probing maidens. It took India 26 balls to score their first run. Rahul was the beneficiary of some Kiwi largesse when New Zealand declined to review an LBW appeal off Henry. Replays indicated three reds. The hosts had already burnt a review on Rahul off Jamieson. It angered Henry, who tossed his jumper into the boundary hoardings when he saw the replay.Jaiswal was hardly secure himself. After an edged boundary, he was reprieved on six when Phillips failed to hold a sharp chance at gully off Jamieson. India went to tea at 16 for no loss after eight overs.On resumption, they cashed in. Jaiswal drove with authority and punished anything loose. He was also eager to bring some of his white-ball audacity into the Test arena, driving on the up, twice miscuing attempted slogs and ramping two fours over the slip cordon.He raced to his fifty and then ramped another boundary to bring up the century partnership. Barring South Africa, Jaiswal now has a 50-plus score in his first Test in the other three SENA countries.Rahul was the perfect foil, playing late, leaving judiciously and playing inside the line. He also put away anything directed at his pads. Their 130-run stand was India’s first century opening partnership in 17 Tests and their first in New Zealand since 1994.Jaiswal appeared set for a hundred before Henry finally won the battle. With wicketkeeper Tom Blundell standing up, Jaiswal nicked one behind. The appeal was turned down, but Henry screamed, “Big noise. Huge noise.” Latham reviewed this time and the spike on replay proved him right.Rahul, playing his first Test in New Zealand, then completed his fifty and became the only Indian opener with a 50-plus score in all SENA countries. He and Devdutt Padikkal ensured there was no late drama.Earlier, Phillips and Nicholls had threatened to bat India out of the contest. Resuming at 243 for five, the pair stretched their sixth-wicket partnership to 216. Phillips completed only his second Test hundred and became only the second batter after Rohit Sharma, against Sri Lanka in 2017, to score hundreds in all three formats against the same opposition in a calendar year.Nicholls, meanwhile, converted his hundred into a monumental unbeaten 175. India struggled for penetration with the second new ball before Akash Deep broke the partnership. Using the width of the crease, he created an angle against Phillips, and the ball held its line just enough to hit the stump, ending an outstanding knock of 118 off 216 balls.The last four wickets fell for just 30, restricting New Zealand to 368.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: IND vs NZ 1st Test: Akash Deep 2.0 is better, smarter and stronger
articles.summary: Even after receiving the generous acknowledgement of “well bowled” from Glenn Phillips, Akash Deep wasn’t quite ready to celebrate.
articles.body: Even after receiving the generous acknowledgement of “well bowled” from Glenn Phillips, Akash Deep wasn’t quite ready to celebrate. The New Zealand centurion had just been castled by a beauty, but the Dehri-born Bengal pacer first looked back at umpire Kumar Dharmasena to check whether his front foot had landed all right. Only after getting the nod from the Sri Lankan did Akash allow himself a celebration.Akash had good reason to look back and check. On his Test debut in Ranchi in Feb 2024, he had sent Zak Crawley’s off-stump cartwheeling, only for his joy to be cut short by the dreaded noball siren after umpire Rod Tucker got the message in his ear-piece from who else, but Dharmasena that Akash had overstepped. For someone who had waited so long for his India cap, after even having to fight with his late father for the right to pursue cricket instead of taking up a job, the wait for a maiden Test wicket was extended by a few more overs.His career since has followed a similarly stop-start path. One of the heroes of India’s 2-2 series draw in England, highlighted by his 10-wicket haul at Edgbaston in Aug 2025, Akash’s struggle-filled journey of economic hardship, grief and relentless hustle took another turn when he suffered a stress fracture of the back while playing the Ranji Trophy semifinal against Jammu & Kashmir in Kalyani last Feb.Just two months earlier, Kolkata Knight Riders had picked him up for Rs 1 crore after Lucknow Super Giants, who had paid Rs 8 cr for him, released him. Following surgery and months of rehabilitation at the Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, Akash was grateful for the trust and support shown by the Indian team management.On Friday, returning to Test cricket after a 15-month hiatus, he repaid that faith with 3-53 from 23 overs. His previous Test appearance had come against England at the Oval.“GG sir (head coach Gautam Gambhir) used to follow up during that period and he would keep asking, ‘kaisa chal raha hain?’” Akash said after the day’s play. “During that time, I worked on my bowling and on areas I could improve. I wanted to get stronger. It didn’t feel like I was playing international cricket after nearly one and a half years.”Perhaps that was because Akash had already put plenty of miles into his legs. He bowled 23.2 overs in the Irani Cup against Rest of India in Srinagar, followed by 33 overs for Bengal against Delhi at Kalyani. He then delivered 35.3 overs in the first India A-New Zealand A game in Lincoln and another 23 in the second in Christchurch.Apart from rehabilitation at the COE, Akash used his time away to work on his craft. In 11 Tests, Akash has 31 wickets, with 11 of those victims bowled. Harry Brook, Joe Root, Zak Crawley, Ben Duckett and Ollie Pope feature on an impressive list of batters whose defences Akash has breached.Phillips, though, might rank as the best of the lot. Akash went wide on the crease and angled the ball in. After pitching, it moved away sharply to beat Phillips and rearrange his stumps. It was Bumrahesque, but Akash describes it matter-of-factly.“The ball wasn’t doing much, so I was trying to move wider of the crease to play with the mind of the batter. I was trying to make the batter play. So I went out. The batter started to play me, whereas he was leaving me earlier. Then I switched again, and got the wicket. I was trying to play with the batters’ mind,” Akash said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Making my job easier': CSK head coach Zaheer Khan breaks silence on MS Dhoni's 'unexpected' retirement
articles.summary: Chennai Super Kings head coach Zaheer Khan has admitted that MS Dhoni's decision to retire from playing in the Indian Premier League came as a surprise to
articles.body: Chennai Super Kings head coach Zaheer Khan has admitted that MS Dhoni's decision to retire from playing in the Indian Premier League came as a surprise to him, while describing the end of the former captain's playing career as an emotional moment for the franchise.Dhoni will no longer take the field for CSK but will remain associated with the five-time champions as their team mentor from IPL 2027. Zaheer said the team would miss having Dhoni as a player but was looking forward to working with him in his new role."It's been an emotional week for all of us, with mixed feelings. Every year, you're hoping that MS is going to be seen playing a role for the team this season. He will be, but in a different avatar, and hence the mixed feelings."I think the journey he has had in cricket has been amazing. Srinivasan rightly said that there is no CSK without MS, and that surely is the case," Zaheer said in a video uploaded on CSK's YouTube channel.Dhoni's retirement from playing was confirmed on November 17, when CSK announced that he would take up the role of team mentor.Zaheer said he was also looking forward to having Dhoni's experience and guidance as he takes charge of the team ahead of the next season."It's mixed feelings for me personally because you're not going to see him as part of the playing team. But I'm excited that he's going to be sharing the burden with me, making my job easier, guiding us in the right direction and being a mentor to us."So, yeah, excited about that, looking ahead, but also emotional about the decision he has taken," Zaheer added.Dhoni led CSK to five IPL titles and two Champions League T20 crowns. However, he did not play a single match during the 2026 season because of fitness concerns.While CSK owner Rupa Gurunath had earlier revealed that Dhoni had indicated he might not return as a player, Zaheer said he had not seriously considered the possibility. His focus, he explained, had been on preparing the squad and planning for the upcoming season."Not at all. I think, for a couple of reasons, it was the last year of this cycle. So maybe, looking ahead at a fresh cycle, those kind of thoughts would have popped into my head," Zaheer said."But right now, I wasn't even thinking about it. Obviously, you're looking at the season, you're looking at the stack-up of your team, the playing XI. I haven't personally given it a thought because, you know, it's MS. He knows what is the right thing to do and when is the time to act upon a certain thing."So I was not really spending my time and energy going in that direction. Whatever it is, it's going to be his decision. I'm planning for the season."So, yes, it was unexpected for me personally when he did mention it in a very, very subtle way, as you know, he doesn't like to create massive news out of it. It just was in the discussion, casually mentioning that, okay, this is it, you're going to have some extra money to go into the auction with," Zaheer added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: KL Rahul added another milestone to his Test career on Saturday with his 13th century in the format.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: KL Rahul added another milestone to his Test career on Saturday with his 13th century in the format. The right-hander reached the landmark on Day 3 of the first Test against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve in Wellington.Rahul completed his hundred with a single off pacer Jacob Duffy. It was his second Test century this year, having scored 100 against Afghanistan at Mullanpur earlier.With 12 Test centuries as an opener, Rahul is now three ahead of Gautam Gambhir and Rohit Sharma, who scored nine each.He is level with Murali Vijay at the third spot on the list, behind only Sunil Gavaskar (33) and Virender Sehwag (22).Rahul among India's most successful Test openersOnly Sunil Gavaskar and Virender Sehwag have scored more Test hundreds as openers for India than Rahul.Most Test hundreds as an opener for India33 – Sunil Gavaskar22 – Virender Sehwag12 – Murali Vijay12 – KL Rahul9 – Gautam Gambhir9 – Rohit SharmaGavaskar tops the list with 33 centuries, followed by Sehwag with 22. Rahul and Vijay have 12 hundreds each, while Gambhir and Rohit finished with nine apiece as openers.Rahul among top openers since 2021Rahul has also been among the most consistent openers in Test cricket since 2021.He has scored seven centuries during this period, putting him level with England's Ben Duckett, India's Yashasvi Jaiswal and Sri Lanka's Dimuth Karunaratne.Most Test hundreds as an opener since 20217 – Ben Duckett7 – Yashasvi Jaiswal7 – Dimuth Karunaratne7 – KL RahulHe has also been among the leading century-makers in the ongoing 2025-27 World Test Championship (WTC) cycle. Rahul, New Zealand captain Tom Latham and Australia's Travis Head have scored four hundreds each as openers, the most in the current cycle.Rahul achieves rare SENA milestoneRahul's Wellington century also brought him a special distinction. He became the first Indian opener to score Test hundreds in all four SENA countries - South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.It was his maiden Test century in New Zealand and his seventh hundred across the four countries.Rahul is the fifth Indian batter to achieve this feat after Mohammad Azharuddin, Sachin Tendulkar, Rahul Dravid and Virat Kohli.Former Sri Lanka captain Kumar Sangakkara and former Pakistan batters Saeed Anwar and Younis Khan have also scored Test centuries in all four SENA countries.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
